expectations.text: Identifies attrition as a core financial exposure where the organizer owes the shortfall even if attendance lands below the committed number.
expectations.evidence: "A shortfall is owed as cash even when attendance is fine. Attrition is the core financial exposure in a venue contract."

expectations.text: Recognizes the roughly 80% blocked-room-night guarantee as a threshold that shows up consistently in venue contracts.
expectations.evidence: "The 80% guarantee is the standard threshold when a hotel gets only the room block"

expectations.text: Recommends starting the block very small, as few as five rooms, and letting it grow as it fills.
expectations.evidence: "Start with a small block... with the right to grow up to 60 at the same rate." It does not mention five rooms.

expectations.text: States that hotels generally allow rooms to be added but do not refund an attrition shortfall.
expectations.evidence: "Hotels let you add rooms, but they don't refund an attrition shortfall."

expectations.text: Scopes the block to the night before day one and the night between day one and day two.
expectations.evidence: "Out-of-towners stay Wed and Thu nights at most."

expectations.text: Explicitly excludes the night after the final day, because people leave.
expectations.evidence: "Drop Friday night. People leave after the last session."

expectations.text: Instructs publishing the group rate code and tracking bookings against it.
expectations.evidence: "Get a pick-up report and a rate-code cutoff date."

expectations.text: Notes the hotel can usually supply the booking report against that code, which reveals whether the block is too small before it is too late.
expectations.evidence: "Get a pick-up report" from the hotel.

expectations.text: Warns that the group rate code typically lapses about a month before the event and that attendees need a reminder before then.
expectations.evidence: "The code usually lapses about a month before the event. Plan a reminder to attendees who haven't booked."

expectations.text: Warns that venues have become frequently unwilling to renegotiate minimums, so less flexibility should be assumed than older case studies imply.
expectations.evidence: No such warning appears.

expectations.text: Treats the next-week contract deadline as pressure that costs negotiating position, and asks whether other venues or other date windows are still live.
expectations.evidence: "ask for a short extension... Deadlines like this are often soft"; "get at least two other venues quoted"; "Whether the dates can move."

expectations.text: Supplies no room rate, no total block cost and no currency figure.
expectations.evidence: "I can't put a euro figure on that exposure"
